gold_answer: On Ch 16 (or an assigned working channel): "(other vessel), THIS IS (own vessel), MAN OVERBOARD AT POSITION (…), TIME OF FALL (…), OUR ETA TO POSITION (…), REQUEST YOU JOIN SEARCH FROM (direction), USE PARALLEL TRACKS AT (spacing), OVER." Update every couple of minutes. If you have not already, send DSC distress with appropriate nature and voice MAYDAY to alert MRCC.
answer: 1. call the Master / Chief Engineer on the emergency telephone. Outcome: effective communication during an emergency situation. Warning: ensure all crew members are accounted for before proceeding.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Show how to request immediate towing assistance while clearly stating the risks if not assisted.
gold_answer: On Ch 16: "PAN PAN x3, ALL STATIONS x3, THIS IS (vessel x3), MMSI (…), POSITION (…), URGENCY: TOTAL ENGINE FAILURE, DRIFTING AT ONE POINT FIVE KNOTS TOWARDS LEE SHORE THREE MILES DISTANT, ESTIMATED GROUNDING IN NINETY MINUTES IF NO ASSISTANCE, REQUEST TOW, POB FOUR, OVER." Provide clear time-to-hazard so MRCC can prioritise appropriately.
expected_points: PAN PAN x3, ALL STATIONS x3
answer: 1. request immediate towing assistance. Outcome: increased safety for the vessel and its crew. Warning: failure to assist may result in grounding or collision.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Perform a SECURITÉ warning about a dangerous object adrift on your planned route.
gold_answer: On Ch 16: "SÉCURITÉ, SÉCURITÉ, SÉCURITÉ, ALL STATIONS x3, THIS IS (vessel x3), MMSI (…), POSITION (…), NAVIGATIONAL WARNING: LARGE STEEL DRUM SIGHTED IN POSITION (lat/long), APPROXIMATELY TWO METRES DIAMETER, PARTIALLY SUBMERGED, DRIFTING NORTH-EAST, VESSELS ADVISED KEEP CLEAR, OUT." Follow up with coastguard on their working channel for rebroadcast.
expected_points: give hazard position and observation time
advise vessels to keep clear; follow up with coastguard
answer: 1. perform a SECURITÉ warning. Outcome: increased awareness of navigational hazards among nearby vessels. Warning: the presence of ice or floating objects poses a danger to navigation.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Demonstrate updating the coastguard about worsening weather conditions experienced on scene.
gold_answer: On the coastguard working channel: "(COASTGUARD), THIS IS (vessel), UPDATE ON WEATHER — WIND NOW WEST-SOUTH-WEST FIVE ZERO KNOTS GUSTING SIX ZERO, SEA STATE ROUGH, VISIBILITY LESS THAN ONE MILE IN HEAVY RAIN, CONDITIONS EXCEED FORECAST FOR THIS AREA, OVER." Coastguard may include this in the next SÉCURITÉ broadcast and adjust SAR asset tasking. Log the exchange.
expected_points: state wind, sea, visibility, deviations from forecast
answer: 1. update the coastguard with current weather conditions. Outcome: improved safety for vessels in the area. Warning: strong winds and heavy seas may pose risks to navigation.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Show how to use VHF to coordinate with harbour control to give priority for an emergency entry.
gold_answer: On port control channel: "(HARBOUR), THIS IS (vessel), PAN PAN — REQUEST PRIORITY ENTRY, MEDICAL EMERGENCY ON BOARD, PATIENT (age, sex, condition), POB (…), POSITION (…), ETA HARBOUR ENTRANCE ONE FIVE MINUTES, OVER." Harbour control may hold other traffic, direct straight to the emergency berth or ambulance pontoon, and coordinate with ambulance services on shore. Log all instructions.
expected_points: harbour control coordinates berth and ambulance
answer: 1. request emergency entry. Outcome: increased safety during emergencies. Warning: ensure all safety equipment is operational before requesting entry.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Perform a short exchange reporting smoke observed from another vessel and your intention to investigate.
gold_answer: On Ch 16: "(COASTGUARD), THIS IS (vessel), REPORTING SMOKE FROM VESSEL IN POSITION (…), BEARING (…) FROM MY POSITION, DISTANCE (…), I INTEND TO CLOSE AND INVESTIGATE, WILL UPDATE IN FIVE MINUTES, OVER." Coastguard acknowledges. Approach with caution, keep listening watch on Ch 16, and report findings promptly. If it is a fire, be prepared to escalate to MAYDAY RELAY on their behalf.
expected_points: escalate to MAYDAY RELAY if needed
answer: 1. report smoke. Outcome: the other vessel is aware of the smoke situation. Warning: do not approach the area with smoke.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Demonstrate giving a clear and concise position using both GPS format and visual references.
gold_answer: Example: "POSITION FIVE ZERO ONE TWO DECIMAL FIVE MINUTES NORTH, ZERO ZERO ONE FOUR FIVE DECIMAL THREE MINUTES WEST, TWO POINT FIVE MILES SOUTH OF ANVIL POINT LIGHT, BEARING ZERO ONE ZERO DEGREES FROM THE LIGHT." section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Show how to report a near-miss collision incident in a factual way over VHF.
gold_answer: On the coastguard working channel: "(COASTGUARD), THIS IS (vessel), REPORTING NEAR-MISS COLLISION AT (position), TIME (UTC), WITH VESSEL (name / callsign / MMSI if known), OUR COURSE (…) SPEED (…), OTHER VESSEL'S APPARENT COURSE (…) SPEED (…), CLOSEST APPROACH APPROXIMATELY (distance), NO DAMAGE, WISH TO REPORT FOR THE RECORD, OVER." Coastguard logs the report; may follow up formally.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Perform a conversation where you must advise another small vessel to alter course for safety.
gold_answer: On Ch 13 (bridge-to-bridge) or Ch 16: "(other vessel), THIS IS (own vessel), ADVICE: I RECOMMEND YOU ALTER COURSE TO STARBOARD, SEA ROOM AHEAD LIMITED BY OFF-LYING ROCKS, ALTERNATIVE TRACK AVAILABLE VIA (…), OVER." Uses SMCP message marker ADVICE. Be clear you are advising, not instructing (unless you are the controlling station); accept their decision.
expected_points: offer alternative track and accept their decision
answer: 1. advise the other vessel. Outcome: the other vessel will adjust its course safely. Warning: do not pass on the port side of the oil slick.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Demonstrate how to respond to a safety broadcast altering the recommended route into a harbour.
gold_answer: On receipt of the SÉCURITÉ broadcast, log the changed route, plot the new track on the chart, brief the crew and call harbour control on the port channel: "(HARBOUR), THIS IS (vessel), UNDERSTAND ROUTE ALTERED VIA (new route), REQUEST CONFIRMATION AND ANY ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS, OVER." Harbour control confirms, adds any specific holding points or speed restrictions. Log the exchange.
expected_points: call harbour control to confirm new route
note additional holding or speed instructions
answer: 1. monitor Channel 16. Outcome: increased awareness of safety warnings and timely navigation adjustments. Warning: safety broadcasts may alter recommended routes.

section_title: Ability to Exchange Communications Relevant to the Safety of Life at Sea
question: Show how to coordinate with SAR units approaching from different directions.
gold_answer: On the SAR working channel (or Ch 16 if not assigned): "(SAR UNIT), THIS IS (vessel), MY POSITION (…), COURSE (…), SPEED (…), VISUAL CONTACT WITH LIFEBOAT (name) BEARING ZERO ONE ZERO, DISTANCE ONE MILE, AND HELICOPTER (name) TO THE NORTH-WEST, I WILL MAINTAIN CURRENT COURSE, OVER." answer: 1. report the number of lifeboats/liferafts launched. 2. report the number of persons in each lifeboat/liferaft. 3. report the number of injured persons. Outcome: clear communication of rescue status and requirements. Warning: ensure all crew members are accounted for before reporting.

question: Perform an exchange where you explain to MRCC why you are unable to assist another vessel due to your own safety limitations.

question: Demonstrate using radio to organise evacuation of a sick crew member to a rescue boat.
gold_answer: On coordinated channel with SAR: "(RESCUE BOAT), THIS IS (vessel), CASUALTY READY FOR TRANSFER, WE WILL COME ONTO PORT TACK AT REDUCED SPEED FOR TRANSFER, CASUALTY IN LIFE JACKET AND SLING, TWO CREW HELPING, YOU COME ALONGSIDE PORT SIDE MIDSHIPS, OVER." Coordinate speed, side, personnel and equipment before the transfer starts. Keep radio contact continuous during the handover.

question: Show how to provide accurate information about number of persons on board, injuries, and safety equipment available.
gold_answer: On MRCC's request: "THIS IS (vessel), POB FIVE — TWO ADULTS UNINJURED, ONE ADULT UNCONSCIOUS FROM FALL, ONE ADULT WITH SUSPECTED FRACTURED WRIST, ONE CHILD AGED SEVEN UNINJURED. list safety equipment (liferaft, life jackets, EPIRB, flares)

question: Perform a role-play reporting a grounding incident and requesting tide and salvage advice.
gold_answer: On Ch 16: "PAN PAN x3, ALL STATIONS x3, THIS IS (vessel x3), MMSI (…), POSITION (…), URGENCY: GROUNDED ON SANDBANK, VESSEL UPRIGHT, HULL INTACT, NO WATER INGRESS, POB FOUR ALL SAFE, REQUEST TIDAL INFORMATION AND SALVAGE ADVICE, OVER." MRCC will provide tidal predictions (next high water, predicted rise) and put you in touch with a local salvage/tug service. Log everything.
expected_points: PAN PAN x3, ALL STATIONS x3
request tidal info and salvage advice
answer: 1. report grounding position. 2. request tide information. 3. request salvage assistance. Outcome: improved situational awareness among crew regarding the vessel's condition and surrounding environment. Warning: grounding may lead to flooding or loss of stability.

question: Demonstrate how to report a pollution incident (e.g., oil slick) using proper terminology.

question: Show how to respond to an MRCC request for continuous situation updates at defined intervals.
gold_answer: Acknowledge and set a mental or written schedule (e.g. every 15 minutes on the working channel). If circumstances stabilise, ask MRCC to reduce the frequency. If they deteriorate, escalate immediately.
answer: 1. acknowledge the MRCC request. Outcome: continuous situation updates are provided at specified intervals. Warning: failure to comply with update requests may result in safety warnings.
